Build an event rate panel from interval and event data

Source: R/event_rate.R
build_event_panel.Rd

Device failure counts cannot be compared directly: online records may overlap, and maintenance (or other excluded) periods should not count as exposure. build_event_panel() computes effective exposure and event counts for event rate analysis:

  1. The online coverage intervals of each device are merged (unioned), so overlapping records are not double-counted.

  2. The exclusion intervals (e.g. maintenance periods) are subtracted from the merged coverage.

  3. The remaining coverage is clipped to the reporting period.

  4. For each device and remaining segment, the effective exposure and the number of events are computed. All boundaries are treated as half-open, [start, end): an event exactly at a segment start is counted, while an event exactly at a segment end is not.

Events are deduplicated by their stable ID: retries of the same event are counted only once. If the same event ID is recorded with conflicting device or time values, build_event_panel() errors.

Devices with positive effective exposure but no events are retained with an event count of zero. Devices with no effective exposure at all are dropped—no zero rate is fabricated for them—and are listed in the dropped component.

Usage

build_event_panel(
  online,
  events,
  exclude = NULL,
  period,
  exposure_unit = NULL,
  device = "device",
  id = "event_id",
  time = "time",
  start = "start",
  end = "end"
)

# S3 method for class 'event_panel'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

online

A data frame of online coverage intervals with columns giving the device, the interval start, and the interval end. Intervals may overlap.

events

A data frame of events with columns giving the device, a stable event ID, and the event time. Rows sharing an event ID are treated as retries of the same event and counted once; conflicting device or time values for the same ID raise an error.

exclude

An optional data frame of exclusion intervals (e.g. maintenance periods), structured like online, to subtract from the merged online coverage.

period

A vector of length 2, c(start, end), giving the reporting period. Only coverage inside this window counts as exposure, and only events inside it are counted. Boundaries are half-open.

exposure_unit

The unit in which exposure is expressed. For Date or POSIXct time variables, one of "seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days" (the default), or "weeks". For numeric time variables, a single positive number giving the number of native time units per exposure unit (default 1).

device, id, time, start, end

Strings naming the device column (shared by all inputs), the event ID column, the event time column, and the interval start and end columns.

x

For the print method, an event_panel object.

...

For the print method, additional arguments (currently ignored).

Value

An object of class event_panel, a list with components:

  • contributions: A tibble with one row per device and effective segment: the device, a segment index, the segment start and end, the effective exposure (in exposure_units), and the number of events attributed to the segment.

  • attribution: A tibble with one row per unique event: the event ID, device, and time, the segment it was attributed to (NA if it fell outside every effective segment), and whether it was counted.

  • duplicates: Rows of events removed as retries of an already counted event ID.

  • dropped: Devices with no effective exposure in the reporting period.

See also

specify_event_rate() to declare a model for the panel, and fit_event_rate() for the one-shot workflow.

Other event rate functions: fit_event_rate(), specify_event_rate()

Examples

online <- data.frame(
  device = c("a", "a", "b"),
  start = c(0, 5, 0),
  end = c(10, 15, 8)
)
events <- data.frame(
  device = c("a", "a", "b"),
  event_id = c("e1", "e1", "e2"),
  time = c(3, 3, 7)
)

# `a` is covered on [0, 15) after merging, `b` on [0, 8);
# the retry of `e1` is counted once
build_event_panel(online, events, period = c(0, 20))
#> # Event rate panel
#> Devices with exposure: 2 (2 segments)
#> Exposure unit: native time units
#> Events: 2 counted / 2 unique (1 duplicate retries removed)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   device segment start   end exposure events
#>   <chr>    <int> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>  <int>
#> 1 a            1     0    15       15      1
#> 2 b            1     0     8        8      1
